User.title: User
User.description: Represents a user of the Course Central system, either a student or a teacher.

name.description: The full name of the user.

email.description: The email address of the user.

role.description: The role of the user (Student or Teacher).

Course.title: Course
Course.description: Represents a course offered in the Learning Management System.

description.description: A brief description of the course.

duration.description: The duration of the course (e.g., number of weeks).

teacherId.description: Reference to the User (Teacher) who created the course. (Relationship: User 1:N Course)

Enrollment.title: Enrollment
Enrollment.description: Represents the enrollment of a student in a course.

id.description: Unique identifier for the enrollment record.

studentId.description: Reference to the User (Student) enrolled in the course. (Relationship: User 1:N Enrollment)

courseId.description: Reference to the Course the student is enrolled in. (Relationship: Course 1:N Enrollment)

enrollmentDate.description: The date the student enrolled in the course.

Assignment.title: Assignment
Assignment.description: Represents an assignment for a specific course.

courseId.description: Reference to the Course the assignment belongs to. (Relationship: Course 1:N Assignment)

description.description: A description of the assignment instructions.

dueDate.description: The due date for the assignment.

Submission.title: Submission
Submission.description: Represents a student's submission for an assignment.

assignmentId.description: Reference to the Assignment the submission is for. (Relationship: Assignment 1:N Submission)

studentId.description: Reference to the User (Student) who submitted the assignment. (Relationship: User 1:N Submission)

submissionDate.description: The date and time the assignment was submitted.

content.description: The content of the submission (e.g., a link to a file or text).

Grade.title: Grade
Grade.description: Represents the grade given to a student for an assignment submission.

submissionId.description: Reference to the Submission the grade is for. (Relationship: Submission 1:1 Grade)

teacherId.description: Reference to the User (Teacher) who gave the grade. (Relationship: User 1:N Grade)

grade.description: The grade given for the submission (e.g., a number between 0 and 100).

feedback.description: Feedback provided by the teacher on the submission.

firestore.reasoning:
The Firestore structure is designed to ensure Authorization Independence, support QAPs, and maintain data integrity. It leverages path-based ownership for user-specific data and denormalization where necessary to avoid complex security rules.  The structure segregates data based on access requirements (e.g., user profiles, course-related data), promoting a homogeneous security posture within each collection.

- `/users/{userId}`: Stores user profiles. Access is restricted to the user themselves and potentially admins (roles managed outside the scope of these entities, potentially via a separate `/roles_admin/{uid}` collection as existence-based global roles).
- `/courses/{courseId}`: Stores course information.  Teachers can create courses, and students can enroll in them. Authorization to create a course is based on the user's teacher role (again, enforced via a separate `/roles_teacher/{uid}` existence check).
- `/users/{userId}/enrollments/{enrollmentId}`: Tracks course enrollments for each user. Authorization relies on the `userId` path segment.
- `/courses/{courseId}/assignments/{assignmentId}`: Stores assignments for each course. Teachers who created the course can create assignments.
- `/users/{userId}/submissions/{submissionId}`: Stores student submissions. Authorization relies on the `userId` path segment, ensuring only the student can create submissions for themselves. `assignmentId` and `courseId` are denormalized into the submission document for querying and display purposes.  These denormalized fields facilitate efficient listing of submissions for a given assignment or course without requiring collection group queries.
- `/courses/{courseId}/grades/{gradeId}`: Stores grades for submissions, teacherId who gave the grade are denormalized.

This design enables simple and robust security rules by:

1.  **Authorization Independence:**  Avoiding `get()` calls by using path-based ownership (e.g., `/users/{userId}/submissions/{submissionId}`) and denormalizing authorization-related data into documents.
2.  **Clarity of Intent:**  Making access control explicit through the structure.  For example, submissions are always owned by a user, simplifying rules.
3.  **QAPs (Rules are not Filters):**  Supporting secure `list` operations by segregating data based on ownership and access requirements.
